\label{lemma-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is affine, then the descent datum is
effective.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. If $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ and each $X_i\to S_i$ is an affine morphism, then the datum is effective: there is an $S$-scheme $X$ and compatible isomorphisms $X\times_SS_i\simeq X_i$. In fact one may construct $X$ by faithfully flat descent of the quasi-coherent algebras defining the affine morphisms.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves effectiveness of every scheme descent datum with affine local morphisms Vi→Xi along any fpqc covering of S, not requiring affine base S or all Vi themselves affine.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. If $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ and each $X_i\to S_i$ is an affine morphism, then the datum is effective: there is an $S$-scheme $X$ and compatible isomorphisms $X\times_SS_i\simeq X_i$. In fact one may construct $X$ by faithfully flat descent of the quasi-coherent algebras defining the affine morphisms.
hypotheses: fpqc cover and a scheme descent datum whose local structure maps are affine.

\label{lemma-closed-immersion}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is a closed immersion, then the descent datum is
effective.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. Suppose $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering and every morphism $X_i\to S_i$ is a closed immersion. Then $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is effective: it comes from a scheme over $S$, because each closed immersion is affine and fpqc descent data for affine morphisms are effective.
